children: President Donald Trump said Sunday that his proposed triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery will be redesigned as a military facility capable of housing drones, snipers and ammunition.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he approved the conversion at the “strong request” of the U.S. military and for national security purposes. He described the project as a “top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch” with drones stored inside and snipers positioned on its roof and surrounding plaza.

Trump didn’t identify the military officials who requested the changes or explain what threats the facility would address. The Pentagon hasn’t publicly released operational details about the proposal.
The president also said large quantities of sniper ammunition would be stored at the complex, which he predicted would be unlike any other facility in the world.

The 250-foot arch is planned for Memorial Circle, which Trump referred to in his post as “Receptive Circle.” The site is at the western end of Arlington Memorial Bridge, between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

The National Park Service originally described the arch as a monument commemorating the 250th anniversary of American independence. Inspired by Roman triumphal arches, it was intended to celebrate the country’s founding principles and serve as a ceremonial gateway to the capital. The agency’s public description doesn’t yet mention drones, snipers or ammunition storage. National Park Service

The proposed structure would be clad in granite and topped by golden statues. Earlier plans also included an observation deck. Excavation was expected to begin this month, with construction projected to take two to three years. CBS News

Trump’s announcement leaves unanswered whether the new military functions would alter the arch’s design, cost, construction schedule or planned public access. It also isn’t clear which branch of the military would operate the facility or what types of drones would be kept there.

The project had already drawn objections from preservationists, veterans and Democratic lawmakers. Critics have argued that the arch could disrupt historic sightlines connecting the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge and Arlington National Cemetery. A pending federal lawsuit also challenges whether the administration has the required congressional authorization.

Trump has promoted the arch as a landmark that would place Washington alongside other world capitals with monumental gateways. In his latest post, he said it would be both a national symbol and a defensive installation, declaring that Washington would have “by far, the greatest” triumphal arch in the world.
